quote: went to jail for two years over a series of perjuries and lies that started with a £36, 6-mph-over speeding ticket
content: The details are wrong in a way that shows the anecdote was not checked. Einfeld was an Australian judge fined in Australian dollars, A$77, for driving at 60 km/h in a 50 zone in Sydney in 2006; the essay gives a British currency and an American unit. He was sentenced in 2009 to three years with a two-year non-parole period, for perjury and perverting the course of justice in claiming that a dead friend had been driving. The essay's own last sentence concedes that "obvious selective reporting is at work in our hearing about this one," which is right and leaves the essay with no evidential content: a single vivid case, selected because it was reported, offered as an exemplar of a theory the essay admits it cannot support this way. It is a two-paragraph essay that names its own fallacy and commits it, with the figures garbled.
